Labs are done in class, saved into your course GitHub repo, and submitted by posting your repo link on Courseworks. This page grows week by week.

## Week 1 (Sep 10)

- **[Lab 0a — Getting set up](lab0a.qmd)**: GitHub account, private course repo, LEAP hub · verification notebook: [verify_setup.ipynb](verify_setup.ipynb)
- **[Lab 0b — Python, just enough to start](lab0b_python_basics.ipynb)**: notebooks, numpy, matplotlib, a first look at pandas and xarray
- **[Lab 0c — The climate of NYC](lab0c_nyc_climate.ipynb)**: distributions, a hand-fit 2-parameter model, ERA5 vs CMIP6
- **[Lab 0d — A bucket](lab0d_bucket.ipynb)**: budgets, equilibrium, stepping forward in time

### Reference (optional)

- **[Where our data comes from](getting_the_data.ipynb)**: how the Lab 0c datasets were pulled from NOAA, ERA5 and the CMIP6 cloud archive — useful when you start hunting data for your project

*Want more Python? A fuller treatment of scientific Python for earth data is in the companion course site: [earth-ds-ml.github.io/summer_2026](https://earth-ds-ml.github.io/summer_2026/intro.html).*
